strategies.name: break_and_retest
strategies.entry_summary: Identify an obvious key level such as pre-market high/low, previous day high/low, or 30-minute opening range high/low. Enter only after price breaks the level with strong momentum/volume, retests it, holds it, and prints confirming price action in the breakout direction (bullish confirmation for a .
strategies.exit_summary: Place the stop on the opposite side of the breakout level, often just beyond the confirmation candle or beyond the broken level. Target the next obvious liquidity area such as a previous high/low or supply/demand zone; the speaker also mentions trimming profits and moving the remainder to break-even

variants.variant_label: Long break-and-retest of resistance turned support
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: bullish confirmation after retest, e.g. long lower wick, bullish hammer, dragonfly doji, optional Bookmap buyer/liqu
variants.target_note: next obvious liquidity area above, such as previous high
variants.transcript_quote: price breaks above it, we then want to see price come back down and test it as support. If it can do that, that would be considered a break and retest

variants.variant_label: Short break-and-retest of support turned resistance
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: bearish confirmation after retest, e.g. long upper wick, bearish hammer, gravestone doji, optional Bookmap seller liqu
variants.target_note: next obvious liquidity area below, such as previous low
variants.transcript_quote: price ends up breaking below the support, well now we have the break, we're waiting for price to come back up and retest it as resistance. If it can b

variants.variant_label: Alternative trigger placement on confirmation candle close
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter at the close of the confirmation candle; speaker also notes some examples may look better on a 2-minute chart
variants.transcript_quote: you go short at the close of this 5-minute candle. Stop loss right above there

result.enumeration_note: One strategy only: the video repeatedly teaches the same break-and-retest skeleton; long and short are opposite-direction variants of that single taught setup with mirrored entry/exit logic, not separate independently taught management frameworks.
